data.narrative:
Reflect Orbital is a Series A-stage space and aerospace company founded by Ben Nowack and Tristan Semmelhack that has raised $35.2M to date. The valuation universe includes five public Space & Aerospace comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and eight private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and Planet Labs, though only a narrow subset are directly comparable on stage and valuation tier.

Of three candidate valuation methods, only stage-progression proved applicable. This method uses the $35.2M total raised as a proxy baseline and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A progression to subsequent financing rounds, yielding a $70.4M implied valuation. Peer-median analysis could not be applied due to insufficient same- or adjacent-stage peers with known valuations in the Space & Aerospace sector—14 total peers exist but fewer than three meet narrow comparability filters. Public-comp anchoring using the sector's 27.4x median price-to-sales multiple was inapplicable because private company revenue data is unavailable.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $60M to $81M, with $70M as the central estimate. This range reflects ±15% variance around the stage-progression method. Key uncertainties include the lack of revenue visibility for revenue-multiple validation and the thinness of late-stage private peer data in this sector. Any post-Series A financing decision should incorporate additional data on unit economics and comparative burn profiles before materialization.
